newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Hutu refugees trek back to Rwanda from Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Hutu refugees trek back to Rwanda from Tanzania.

text.p: Thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees are pouring back into their homeland from Tanzania in the second major mass repatriation in five weeks.
"Many people are walking in the right direction," said Anne Willem Bijleveld of the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR on Saturday night. "Things are going in the right direction."

He said 2,000 to 3,000 had crossed into Rwanda by the Rusomo crossing from Tanzania by nightfall and at least an estimated 20,000 more were in a column on the 17-km (10-mile) road east from the border to Benaco camp, the largest in Tanzania.
The exodus followed talks between camp leaders in Benaco and officials of the Tanzanian government, which says it wants all 540,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees in Tanzania out by December 31.
"It looks now as if the army has things under control," said Bijleveld, adding that it had dropped restrictions against the UNHCR assisting in the government's mass repatriation operation.
He said soldiers walked with refugees but "in a humane manner" and even assisted the needy.
It was unclear if the Rusomo crossing would remain open throughout the night but refugees often sleep at the roadside for a few hours during the night before resuming marching at dawn.
Shortly after dark, the International Federation of the Red Cross estimated 500 were crossing every hour. The U.N. World Food Programme put the flow to Rwanda at thousands per hour.
The UNHCR estimated before the column reached the border that hundreds of thousands were streaming towards Rusomo from as far away as Nyakahura, about 100 km (65 miles) to the southeast.
Aid agencies have set up water points, health posts and biscuit distributions along a 100-km (65-mile) route in Rwanda.
About 200,000 of the refugees orignally came from villages within 30 km (18 miles) of the Rusomo crossing and were expected to walk home.
U.N. aid officials said they believed a rush away from the border by hundreds of thousands of refugees on Thursday broke the grip of Hutu intimidators who refuse to go home over innocent refugees.
Troops and police turned back most of the refugees on Friday and authorities said they knew where the remainder were.

It was unclear what would happen to the Hutu militiamen and former troops who oppose returning because of their involvement in the genocide of an estimated 800,000 people in Rwanda in 1994. There are also 112,000 Burundian refugees in Tanzania.
It was the second mass return of Rwandan refugees. More than 500,000 left Zaire in four days from November 15 after a rebellion by Zairean Tutsis broke the Hutu intimidators' hold.
The United Nations has ordered 350 Canadian servicemen and women making up a multinational force for eastern Zaire to pull out and return home from their bases in Uganda and Rwanda.
The force, formed in mid-November, never intervened in eastern Zaire to help Rwandan refugees and failed to win the support of other potential contributors.
Canadian spokesmen said troops would start leaving on Monday and the last members would be home by the end of the month.
African leaders including South Africa's President Nelson Mandela will meet in Nairobi on Monday to discuss efforts to control conflict in Zaire and the Great Lakes region of central Africa.
